Trace plots of MCMC chains

Source: R/plots.R
plot_trace.Rd

Plots the MCMC chains for some of the edge weights of a fitted model, to check that the sampler worked. MCMC (Markov chain Monte Carlo) draws samples from the posterior in several independent runs called chains. The chains should overlap and show no trends; if they don't, the posterior may not be reliable, and running more warmup iterations may help.

Usage

plot_trace(obj, par_ids = 1:5, ...)

Arguments

obj

A fitted bison_model object (fitted with Stan, not a conjugate model).

par_ids

Indices of the edge weights to plot, in the order of get_edgelist(). Indices beyond the number of edges are ignored.

...

Additional arguments passed to plot().

Value

NULL, invisibly. The function is called for its plots.

See also

plot_predictions() for checking model fit.

Examples

sim_data <- simulate_bison_model("binary", aggregated = TRUE)
fit_edge <- bison_model(
  (event | effort) ~ dyad(node_1_id, node_2_id),
  data = sim_data$df_sim, model_type = "binary",
  priors = get_default_priors("binary")
)
#> Running MCMC with 4 parallel chains...
#> 
#> Chain 1 finished in 0.2 seconds.
#> Chain 2 finished in 0.3 seconds.
#> Chain 3 finished in 0.2 seconds.
#> Chain 4 finished in 0.2 seconds.
#> 
#> All 4 chains finished successfully.
#> Mean chain execution time: 0.2 seconds.
#> Total execution time: 0.5 seconds.
#> 
plot_trace(fit_edge, par_ids = 1:4)
